dossier.public_summary: The dip depth varies dramatically between sectors and individual transits and is locked to the star's rapid 3-day spot rotation with huge spot amplitudes. The V-shaped, highly variable signal repeats at the rotation period, so it is stellar variability/cross-talk, not a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes 964.2% between sectors (depth_ppm -228 to 1892) and sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source with p_constant_all=0.0 and p_constant 0.0 for TESS-SPOC. A real planet should be steady apart from calibration, not strongly variable within one source.

Individual transit depths are inconsistent (chi2 12337.01420762046 dof 93, p_consistent 0.0) with outliers at 2891 ppm and -272 ppm and share_of_top_3 0.536. The signal does not represent one stable depth.

Stellar rotation period from every sector 2.89-3.017 d (amplitude_ppm 38734-113630) matches signal period 3.00231 d (signal_over_rotation 1.0136090479405808). Signal at rotation multiple 1 with phase_curve amplitude_ppm 302.8 ratio_to_depth 0.1711 and chi2 1223 dof 9 indicates spot/cross-talk variability, not a planet.
V-shaped transit with shape.v_sigma 20.15 favours a binary/grazing eclipse over a planetary transit despite centroid verdict on_target.
